pronoun_sequence: Ch 11 mē/tē in 2nd-person speech; Ch 14 meus/tuus in adjective agreement; Ch 15 hic/ille in near/far nominated groups; Ch 16 nōs/vōs; Ch 20 is/ea/id with eum/eam/eius; Ch 26 sē/suus contrasted with eius; Ch 81 eum vs sē in ACI.
pronoun_notes: Secondary pronoun application at chapters 14, 15 and 26 is staged in an explicitly marked extra lectio. This is a pacing compromise requiring Latinist review; no new 130 chapter slots are invented.
pronoun_count_policy: Examples like is/eum/eius are inflected forms of one lexeme and must never be counted as three distinct new words. mē/tē and nōs/vōs are forms/persons of pronominal paradigms, not new entries per inflection. Similarly suus/sua/suum is a single headword; sē belongs to the sui reflexive paradigm.
